title: Coturn: struct-field bounds in the internal proofs

blocks.text: Coturn: struct-field bounds in the internal proofs
blocks.subtitle: Findings dossier, source excerpts and paper reuse package

blocks.text: Coturn is a TURN and STUN server implementation. The reviewed target is FuzzStunClient. The ASan and ASan+UBSan coturn proof cases have machine-checked models satisfying the complete original internal invariant while a buffer-derived write address is one byte before the `buf` field. The address is the storage of the preceding `channel[3]` field, within the same `stun_buffer`. See the pinned project README under upstream/coturn/README.md.
Established: non-entailment of the field lower bound by the selected internal invariants. Input reachability, attacker control and downstream corruption are unestablished.

blocks.title: 1. The C objects and the static call context

blocks.text: The declaration has two distinct array fields. `STUN_CHANNEL_HEADER_LENGTH` is 4 and `STUN_BUFFER_SIZE` is 65507. [C1] [C2] [C3]

blocks.caption: stun_buffer declaration

blocks.text: In the audited RV64 layout, `channel` starts at offset 0 and `buf` at offset 4. The remaining offsets are `len` at 65512, `offset` at 65520 and `coffset` at 65522; the whole struct has size 65528 and alignment 8. `checks/layout-rv64.txt` records an independent layout-only Clang check using matching scalar types and declarations.

blocks.caption: Struct wrapper passes its buf field

blocks.text: For the reviewed certificate context, the wrapper passes its array field `buf->buf` and the address of its length field into the `_str` API. The static source call chain continues through `stun_set_channel_bind_request_str`, `stun_attr_add_addr_str`, and `stun_attr_add_str`. The address builder makes the final call at line 1729. This identifies the source field and call context; it is not an input-reachability argument. [C5] [C6]

blocks.caption: Signed message-length result and -1 failure

blocks.text: The signed result is either a validated message length or the failure value -1. Identifying that error value does not establish that this caller can produce it. In particular, the abstract witness is not a proof that this helper returns -1 on the witness memory.

blocks.title: 2. The access and its missing field-bound obligation

blocks.text: The following is the complete body of `stun_attr_add_str`, so the argument normalization, length check, padding and writes remain visible. [C8]

blocks.caption: Complete stun_attr_add_str body
Two-byte write helper

blocks.text: The helper writes two bytes. Let B be the struct base, b = B + 4 the start of `buf`, and p the write destination. In the admitted case, p = b - 1 = B + 3, the storage of `channel[3]`; the second byte is at `buf[0]`. The capacity check on `newlen` is an upper-bound check and does not by itself prove `clen >= 0`.

Required for the two-byte write:  b <= p  and  p + 2 <= b + 65507.
Admitted first-byte address:      p = b - 1.
Enclosing-object address:         p = B + 3, inside the same struct.

Both selectors use zero-based disjunct index 1 and empty inline context. `sp0` is the proof environment stack anchor; the three builds have different frame layouts. `both` is the repository name for ASan+UBSan. [P2] [P3]

In ASan, the selected cut is before the addition that forms x21. The theorem computes the destination as machine-word addition x14+x18. In ASan+UBSan, x25 already holds the destination. The combined build's extra recorded constraints therefore do not restore the field lower bound.

Static instruction inspection places the combined build's pointer checks at 0x8c8b4-0x8c8d4, before its selected cut. The later ASan shadow tests examine zero in the supplied model. These instruction associations are source/binary audit evidence; the new Rocq statements are state-existence theorems, not complete small-step traces through the C operation.

Certificate reference chains are ASan 914 -> 754 at call PC 0x86ae8, then 754 -> 752 at 0x8e380; and ASan+UBSan 1034 -> 847 at 0x86610, then 847 -> 845 at 0x8d6d0. These references identify the reviewed call contexts, without establishing that an input reaches the selected disjunct.
The formal claim

There exist valuation nu, registers R and memory M such that:
  original Gamma_2(case, nu, R, M)
  and rank(case, nu) >= 0
  and destination(R) = b - 1 < b
  and store_ok(M, destination(R), 1) = true
  and ASan shadow(destination(R)) = 0.
Therefore Gamma_2(case) does not entail b <= destination.

The two final statements are `asan_decoded_case_admits_buf_minus_one` at `reproduction/proof/Complete.v:56` and `both_decoded_case_admits_buf_minus_one` at line 127. Each selects the unit, full state and rank from the original compressed certificate and uses the original `unit_params2`/`genv` parameters and the SHA-pinned binary images.

These are literal excerpts from the successful audit sources, not schematic pseudocode. `asan_buffer` and `both_buffer` are the field starts; `asan_destination` is the machine addition x14+x18, and `both_destination` is register x25. The definitions and all witnesses are carried in `reproduction/proof/`.

Theorem asan_decoded_case_admits_buf_minus_one :
 exists U nu regs mem,
  find (fun u => Z.eqb (u_vid (u1 u)) 752) asan_decoded = Some U /\
  select_case asan_decoded 752 0x8d348 = Some asan_case /\
  select_rank asan_decoded 752 0x8d348 = Some asan_rank /\
  gamma2 SEGSA (unit_params2 (genv_asan true) U) asan_E mem
    (load_cstate2 (unit_params2 (genv_asan true) U) asan_case 0x8d348 []) nu regs mem /\
  0 <= eval nu asan_rank /\
  bv_unsigned (asan_destination regs) = asan_buffer-1 /\
  bv_unsigned (asan_destination regs) < asan_buffer /\
  store_ok SEGSA mem (asan_destination regs) 1 = true /\
  rdn SEGSA mem (wordZ (0x7fff8000 + bv_unsigned (asan_destination regs)/8)) 1
    = Some [Z_to_bv 8 0].
blocks.caption: ASan: reproduction/proof/Complete.v:56-68

blocks.text:
Theorem both_decoded_case_admits_buf_minus_one :
 exists U nu regs mem,
  find (fun u => Z.eqb (u_vid (u1 u)) 845) both_decoded = Some U /\
  select_case both_decoded 845 0x8c93c = Some both_case /\
  select_rank both_decoded 845 0x8c93c = Some both_rank /\
  gamma2 SEGSB (unit_params2 (genv_both true) U) both_E mem
    (load_cstate2 (unit_params2 (genv_both true) U) both_case 0x8c93c []) nu regs mem /\
  0 <= eval nu both_rank /\
  bv_unsigned (both_destination regs) = both_buffer-1 /\
  bv_unsigned (both_destination regs) < both_buffer /\
  store_ok SEGSB mem (both_destination regs) 1 = true /\
  rdn SEGSB mem (wordZ (0x7fff8000 + bv_unsigned (both_destination regs)/8)) 1
    = Some [Z_to_bv 8 0].
blocks.caption: ASan+UBSan: reproduction/proof/Complete.v:127-139

blocks.text: `SEGSA` and `SEGSB` are the static images regenerated from the SHA-pinned instrumented ELF files. `store_ok` here checks permission for the first byte; this is enough to exhibit the missing lower bound. These existence statements do not assert a small-step execution to, or through, the write.

blocks.title: 5. Why the internal proof permits the neighboring byte

blocks.text: The complete extended interpretation `gamma2` includes the base invariant, environment, runtime memory, fixed symbols, division definitions, all regions, liveness, symbol bounds, globals, flags and memoized facts. The new witnesses satisfy this entire predicate. [P4] [P5]

Definition gamma2 (mem0 : word -> option byte) (A : vstate2) (nu : val) (regs : bvmap 5 word) (mem : word -> option byte) : Prop :=
    gamma SEGS P1 E1 (zpatch mem0 mem) (v1 A) nu regs mem
    /\ env_ok2 /\ MC2 mem0 mem /\ gamma_fix2 E nu
    /\ gamma_divdef nu A
    /\ (forall r, In r (vs_rgn A) -> region_ok nu A mem r)
    /\ live_ok nu A
    /\ state_below2 A
    /\ globs_ok2 A
    /\ flags_inv A nu mem
    /\ memo_ok nu mem A.
blocks.caption: Complete extended concretization predicate gamma2

blocks.text: For these ordinary SP0-relative accesses, the extended store machinery falls back to the ordinary stack store checker. [P7]

Definition x_store2 (P : vparams2) (A : vstate2) (sz : msize) (rs1 rs2 : Z) (imm : Z) : vresult2 :=
  let n := msize_z sz in
  match addr_of (v1 A) rs1 imm with
  | None => VR2_fail "store via Top address"
  | Some addr =>
      match classify2 A addr n true with
      | None => lift1c A (x_store (p1 P) (v1 A) sz rs1 rs2 imm)
      | Some (C2Fail m) => VR2_fail m
      | Some C2Dead => VR2_next []
      | Some (C2Rgn r off lo hi) => store_rgn A r off lo hi n (get_reg (v1 A) rs2)
      end
blocks.caption: Extended store falls back to ordinary store checker

blocks.text: The ordinary classifier requires the access to be inside the stack window and the unit write set. It does not attach the `buf` field's start address to this pointer. The decoded write intervals in the preceding table explicitly include the byte before `buf`. [P6] [P8]

Definition classify (P : vparams) (A : vstate) (addr : lin) (n : Z) (is_store : bool) : cres :=
  let cs := lcoef addr SP0 in let cd := lcoef addr DATA in
  if Z.eqb cs 1 && Z.eqb cd 0 then
    let off := lsub addr (lsym SP0) in
    (* [comment removed for export] *)
    if negb (qge A off (- vp_frame P)) then
      (if bnd_dead A off then CDead else CFail "stack access below window")
    else if negb (qle A off (- n)) then
      (if bnd_dead A off then CDead else CFail "stack access above sp0")
    else
      let b := bnd A off in
      match b with
      | (Some lo, Some hi) =>
          if itv_empty b then CDead
          else if is_store && negb (in_ranges (vp_wstack P) lo (hi - lo + n)) then CFail "store outside unit write set"
          else COk (RStack off lo hi)
      | _ => CFail "stack offset unbounded"   (* [comment removed for export] *)
blocks.caption: Ordinary stack-window and write-set checks

blocks.text: The extra fake-frame, borrowed-argument, flag and shadow regions are all accounted for in the witnesses. Their existence does not supply the missing bound b <= p at this access. The result follows from the complete predicate, rather than from inspecting only the exported agreement statement.

blocks.title: 6. How this matches Section 4 of the paper

blocks.text: The current Section 4, "An Example", uses `struct S { char buf[20]; unsigned char op; }` and a fill operation that may cross from `buf` into `op`. The modified opcode still selects an in-bounds element of a 256-entry handler table. [M1] The section distinguishes mapped/permitted enclosing storage from the bounds of its finer-grained objects. [M2]

A countermodel to field-bound entailment by the selected internal invariants

blocks.text: The shared point is a subobject boundary that is absent from the effective proof obligation. An address can remain within permitted enclosing storage while violating the bounds of the particular array field from which the pointer was formed. A two-byte write starting one byte before `buf` already violates the field lower bound, even if only its first byte targets the neighboring field.

For UBSan, the paper can use a narrow, checked claim: in this particular ASan+UBSan build and certificate case, the complete retained constraints admit the already formed out-of-field pointer. This does not require a universal claim about every UBSan configuration or every pointer-decay optimization.
The coturn evidence establishes the field-boundary distinction. It does not establish a reachable coturn attack, a changed channel byte, a dispatch effect, or a false published agreement theorem.

blocks.title: 7. Material ready to reuse in the paper

blocks.text: Compact paragraph

Coturn's client-message proofs provide a concrete instance of this field-boundary gap. Its `stun_buffer` places a four-byte `channel` array immediately before a `buf` array. The routine `stun_attr_add_str` forms `attr_start = buf + clen` and writes two bytes there. We machine-checked abstract states admitted by both the ASan and ASan+UBSan internal cut-invariants in which that address is `buf - 1`, the storage of `channel[3]`. These states satisfy the complete original invariant, including its memory permissions and shadow facts. Thus the existing invariants do not establish that this access stays inside the array field. This is a result about the strength of the internal invariants; it does not establish that a covered input reaches the state or changes the program's behavior.

Technical formulation

Let b be the start of `stun_buffer.buf` and p the destination of the first lowered byte store for `turn_write_u16(attr_start, attr)`. Field-level safety requires at least `b <= p`. For ASan unit 752 at cut `0x8d348`, disjunct 1, and ASan+UBSan unit 845 at cut `0x8c93c`, disjunct 1, the new Rocq lemmas construct valuations, registers and memory satisfying the complete original `gamma2` predicate while `p = b - 1`, `store_ok(p, 1) = true` and the corresponding ASan shadow byte is zero. The cases, ranks and relevant unit parameters are checked against the original compressed certificates with the repository's decoder. Consequently, these cut-invariants do not entail the field lower bound. This countermodel does not establish a concrete execution from the harness input, or refute the published agreement theorem.

The paper's current `\repo` macro points to older proof commit 98e995d4. The supplied snippets use their own `\coturnproofrepo` macro pinned to a6839bb9. Do not silently cite the new finding through the older link macro. The supplied bibliography file provides entries for the pinned proof repository and coturn source.

blocks.title: 8. Plain-build evidence and the bzip2 result

blocks.text: Plain coturn case: a distinct evidence level

The plain-build investigation found unit 166, entry 0x18898, cut 0x18994, context [], disjunct 0. Its field start is sp0-65628 and x24 is sp0-65629. The instruction at 0x18998 is `sb x10, 0(x24)` (word 0x00ac0023); the next stored cut at 0x189ac records a one-byte slot at that offset. [P1]

The unit write set contains [-65629,-65585) and [-120,-112), relative to sp0. The selected pure constraints admit s21=12, s23=4, s27=20, s28=8, sp0=0x7fff80000000, DATA=0x400000 and SIZE=1. The corrected congruence for s27 is 4 modulo 8. Slot consistency, pure constraints, instruction bytes and range inclusion were checked by Python.

A certificate reference chain connects root 249 to unit 170 at call PC 0x14c90, then to unit 166 at 0x192f0. These are proof/call references, not a reachability proof for the selected abstract disjunct. This investigation did not add a full original-gamma Rocq existence theorem for the plain variant. The complete decoded data and earlier report are in `evidence/plain-witness.json` and `evidence/plain-audit.txt`.
bzip2: the initially proposed example did not survive internal review

The bzip2 review used the same proof commit and source pin f5dfc96063fef2d9c5446d0733867d899ef9b942. It inventoried 115 fields in the core structs and 24 inline arrays, checked their offsets, lengths and element widths against the RV64 layout, and inspected the associated bounded-access proof families. No concrete omitted field-bound obligation was identified in that source review.

This is a manual-review result, not a newly machine-checked universal C-subobject safety theorem. The completed harness compresses and then decompresses its own output; standalone arbitrary-input decompression and file-I/O API histories have different coverage. Coarsened saved fields concern persistent value/session contracts, not an identified field-overflow counterexample. The full inventory is preserved as `evidence/bzip2-field-bounds-audit.json`.

The bzip2 result is useful methodological context: omission of a property from an exported theorem does not by itself establish that the internal proof omits it. Coturn supplies the stronger evidence because its selected complete internal predicates have explicit checked countermodels.

All 24 core inline arrays in the manual audit are listed below. Sizes and offsets are bytes in the audited RV64 layout. The JSON inventory also records the other 91 scalar/pointer fields and the exact bounded-access proof-family locations for every field. No row is a newly replayed universal field-safety theorem.

The per-field evidence is in `evidence/bzip2-field-bounds-audit.json`. It links to the same current proof commit a6839bb9. The completed bzip2 proof is a source-review contrast to the checked coturn countermodels, rather than a positive missing-field-bound finding.
Correction to the earlier extraction

The first Python decoder parsed a congruence residue as unsigned. The upstream decoder uses the signed parser for the residue: the format is symbol, unsigned modulus, signed residue. [P9] Rocq's equality check against the original certificate exposed the error.

The decoder, decoded data and published witnesses were corrected. The field addresses remain one byte before `buf`, so the final finding is unchanged. The final instrumented source literals and ranks are checked by the original Rocq decoder; the Python translation is not part of the trusted formal check.
Recorded machine check

The original fresh build passed all 88 sources in 166.78 seconds on 1 November 2026 (finished 04:11:52 UTC), using the release-pinned Rocq 9.2 checker with OCaml 4.14.3. The 75 copied coturn dependencies, 11 audit sources and two generated image modules were recompiled. Rocq and LPS libraries are supplied by the pinned checker image. `Print Assumptions` for the final theorems lists 21 allowed Rocq array, integer and string primitives; no new axioms, admitted lemmas or unchecked casts were introduced. The source SHA-256 values match the carried build record.

Rocq checks exact equality of the selected state and rank with the original compressed data. It also checks relevant unit-parameter fields against the decoded unit. The witnesses construct an environment, valuation, registers and concrete memory for every clause of the complete original gamma2 interpretation. `gamma_params_exact` proves that discarding unused static-table fields during computation preserves the entire predicate, and the final theorem statements restore the original parameters.

./run.sh > check.log 2>&1

blocks.text: Claims suitable for the paper

items: The selected complete coturn cut-invariants do not entail the lower bound of the buf array field.
Both instrumented variants have checked invariant models with destination = buf - 1, writable memory there and a zero ASan shadow byte.
This is an internal proof-strength result, stronger evidence than absence of field bounds in an exported theorem statement alone.
The field-boundary distinction matches the within-aggregate point illustrated in Section 4.

blocks.text: Claims not established by this investigation

items: A harness input reaches either abstract state, or makes this helper return -1 in the reviewed caller context.
The channel byte changes, is attacker-controlled, or affects later behavior.
A complete execution through the two-byte C write, a vulnerability, or an exploit.
A counterexample to the published agreement theorem, or a universal result about every coturn access, UBSan configuration, or source-level C object.

blocks.text: The formal result is a non-entailment statement about particular accepted internal predicates. The C correspondence and source layout explain which source-field obligation is absent. These two evidence layers are recorded separately so the paper can state the conclusion at its demonstrated strength.
